name: CARE (Case Report Guidelines)
source: Gagnier JJ, Kienle G, Altman DG, Moher D, Sox H, Riley D; CARE Group. The CARE Guidelines: Consensus-based Clinical Case Reporting Guideline Development. Glob Adv Health Med. 2013;2(5):38-43. https://www.care-statement.org/checklist | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3833570/

items.text: Include the primary diagnosis or intervention and the phrase 'case report' in the title.
Provide 2 to 5 keywords covering key diagnoses or interventions, including 'case report'.
Summarize what is unique about the case and what it adds to medical literature.
State the patient's primary concerns and key clinical findings.
Summarize the main diagnoses, therapeutic interventions, and clinical outcomes.
State the main takeaway lessons from the case report.
Briefly explain why the case is unique, supported by relevant medical literature references.
Provide de-identified patient demographic and case-specific details.
Describe the patient's chief complaints and presenting symptoms.
Summarize relevant medical, family, psychosocial, and genetic history.
Describe relevant past interventions and their clinical outcomes.
Report pertinent physical examination and important clinical findings.
Organize key historical and current care events chronologically in a table or figure.
Describe diagnostic methods used, including examination, lab tests, imaging, or surveys.
Describe diagnostic challenges such as access, cost, language, or cultural factors.
State the final diagnosis and other differential diagnoses considered.
Report prognostic characteristics, such as staging, when applicable.
Specify types of therapeutic interventions used, such as pharmacologic, surgical, or preventive.
Detail intervention administration, including dosage, strength, and duration.
Describe any changes to interventions and the clinical rationale.
Report clinician-assessed and patient-assessed outcomes when available.
Summarize important follow-up diagnostic and test results.
Report intervention adherence and tolerability and how they were assessed.
Report any adverse or unanticipated events.
Discuss strengths and limitations in the clinical management of this case.
Discuss the case in the context of relevant medical literature.
Explain the rationale supporting the conclusions, including causality considerations.
State the primary takeaway lessons in a single-paragraph conclusion without references.
Include the patient's own perspective on the treatments received, when appropriate.
Confirm that the patient provided informed consent for publication, available on request.
